own_solution.law: Independent radioactive decay gives A_s(t)=2400·2^(-t/6) and A_l(t)=500·2^(-t/72), with t in hours. Equal detection efficiencies cancel when the count rates are equated. Thus t=(72/11)log2(2400/500).
assumptions: Count rates mean expected decay count rates.
The stated half-lives govern exponential decay.
The common detection efficiency is nonzero.

uncertain_fields: The time of addition in T45EB is unspecified.

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: T45EB does not specify when the additional batch enters the sample, so the equality time is not uniquely determined.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9D9A and TF3A2 replace the specified 170 Bq with unspecified small amounts, so the activity variants do not preserve the required number and unit.

counterexamples: For T45EB, adding the 170 Bq batch at preparation gives equality at (72/11)log2(2400/670)=12.0489 h; adding it at 24 h leaves the first equality at 14.8126 h, before the addition.
notes: The base problem is well-posed. T7283 increases the initial longer-lived activity to 670 Bq. The counter explicitly detects only decays in this sample, so waste-drum additions and changes confined to an earlier sample are disconnected. Both efficiency sentences specify the same dimensionless value, 0.36, which cancels. No external information was consulted.
